title: tools/gradlew.cjs fails before Gradle starts under NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath
body:
## Summary
tools/gradlew.cjs spawned a bare `gradlew.bat` through cmd, which cannot find it when NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1 is set (agent harnesses set it).

## Description
tools/gradlew.cjs:14 called `spawnSync("gradlew.bat", args, { shell: true })`. cmd resolves a bare name through the current directory only when that variable is unset, so every Windows run of the manifest build/test capabilities (.ai/manifest.yaml:30-31) and the AGENTS.md Gradle rows died with "'gradlew.bat' is not recognized". Fixed: the wrapper is named by its quoted absolute path (and `sh <root>/gradlew` elsewhere). New suite tools/gradlew-test.cjs, wired in repo-guardrails.yml.

## Flow
- agent runs `node tools/gradlew.cjs :core:test` -> cmd /c gradlew.bat -> "not recognized", exit 1
- fix: spawn `"<root>\gradlew.bat"`; test copies the script beside a stub wrapper in a path with a space, env var set

## Expected impact
Every agent and the doctor --run on Windows can run the Gradle capabilities again; Linux CI unchanged (sh path only made absolute).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the Gradle entry starts on a host that does not search the cwd
Before: node tools/gradlew.cjs :core:test exit 1 before Gradle; gradlew-test 0/3
After: exit 0 BUILD SUCCESSFUL; gradlew-test 3/3
Method: gate - red-then-green suite plus the real command
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/gradlew.cjs:14 (before): spawnSync("gradlew.bat", args, { cwd: root, stdio: "inherit", shell: true })
NoDefaultCurrentDirectoryInExePath=1
$ node tools/gradlew.cjs --version -> 'gradlew.bat' is not recognized ... exit=1

title: Desk layering check unwired from CI since it landed red on main; wired back with 3 owed breaks
body:
## Summary
repo-guardrails.yml ran no layering check, while AGENTS.md and .ai/memory/0018 say it goes red on a desk layering break.

## Description
tools/desk-boundaries.cjs was written green on 0158739f (2026-10-05, 142 sources; exit 0 at b195cc9b) and squash-merged in fc866ead (2026-10-20) onto a desk that had grown three breaks: engines/meter.ts -> lib/dataDir.ts (de7361f2), twin/state.ts writes twin.json (c108f638/8832d8ba), rules/docx.ts -> node:zlib (c108f638). The merge unwired the step (.github/workflows/repo-guardrails.yml:23-25 before) instead of baselining, so any new break merged unseen. CI did not "catch" it because the step was removed in the same merge; the suite case 11 was red. Fixed per quality-gates/gate-liveness (retrofit onto an artifact that already violates the rule) and waiver-names-its-finding: OWED entries (rule + file + detail substring + reason) print and do not fail, any other break fails, a stale entry fails.

## Flow
- PR adds a rules/ file importing node:fs -> no workflow ran desk-boundaries -> merges
- fix: OWED list in tools/desk-boundaries.cjs, cases 11-13, suite + check wired in the layering job

## Expected impact
A new layering break goes red on every PR again; the three existing breaks stay visible as OWED until the owner decides (card below).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - new desk layering breaks are blocked
Before: step unwired; desk-boundaries exit 1 with 3 problems; suite 10/13
After: wired; exit 0, 0 problems, 3 owed; suite 13/13; seeded new break -> exit 1; seeded stale OWED -> exit 1
Method: gate - suite red-then-green, seeded controls on a scratch copy of desk/src
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
b195cc9b: desk boundaries 142 files 0 problems exit 0
fc866ead: 236 files 3 problems exit 1
repo-guardrails.yml:23 (before) "# Not wired: tools/desk-boundaries-test.cjs case 11 fails on the current desk"

title: Never-commit guardrail misses desk/.env.local and keystores
body:
## Summary
.ai/guardrails.yaml neverCommit patterns are root-relative git pathspecs, so the doctor hard guardrail did not see desk/.env.local or any keystore.

## Description
.ai/doctor.mjs:209 runs `git ls-files -- <patterns>`; `.env.local` matches only the root file. desk/.env.local is the one secrets file AGENTS.md and the manifest name, and AGENTS.md forbids keystores; neither *.jks nor *.keystore was listed. Fixed: added "*/.env", "*/.env.local", "*.jks", "*.keystore" (0 tracked matches). Case 6 in tools/security-policy-test.cjs runs the real doctor on a scratch index that tracks five seeded secret files.

## Flow
- git add -f desk/.env.local -> doctor guardrail.never-commit pass
- fix: patterns; test seeds 5 files, asserts each named in the fail

## Expected impact
A committed desk/.env.local or keystore now fails conformance-gate on the PR. Could break: a legit file named .env under a subdirectory (none tracked).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the secret guardrail covers the named secret files
Before: seeded files named in the doctor fail: 1 of 5
After: 5 of 5; this tree pass (11 patterns); doctor-gate exit 0
Method: gate - case 6 red-then-green
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence: probe repo: git ls-files -- .env .env.local -> [] ; git ls-files -- "*/.env.local" "*.jks" -> desk/.env.local desk/release.jks

title: SECURITY.md ticked two guardrails no workflow runs

Fixed: comments stripped before matching, a submitted-graph tick needs a dependency-submission step, an "every pull request" tick needs its cited workflow to trigger on pull_request; SECURITY.md reworded.

## Flow
- reader trusts the policy -> believes Gradle alerts are live and the PR doctor runs in ai-conformance
- fix: test strengthened (red on old text), SECURITY.md corrected

## Expected impact
The policy only claims what runs; the next drift fails harness-drills.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no false ticked guardrail
Before: false ticked claims 2; new checks red on old text
After: 0; 6/6; seeded re-citation and "graph is submitted" each exit 1
Method: gate - red-then-green with seeded controls
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten

title: Weekly drift run died on the first engine warning on stderr
body:
## Summary
scripts/model-drift.ps1 ran node with 2>&1 under $ErrorActionPreference=Stop; Windows PowerShell made the first stderr line terminating.

## Description
scripts/model-drift.ps1:29,48 (before). Engines print warnings on exactly the failing calls (desk/src/lib/engines/health.ts:66,83, codex.ts:67, text.ts:97, meter.ts:51), so the run that most needs a record lost it: no verdict in the log, no DRIFT line, exit 1 (read as drift) instead of the run's code. Reproduced in a 5.1 probe. The log also mixed UTF-8 and Tee-Object's UTF-16. Fixed: the run goes under Continue (restored in finally), lines logged as UTF-8 text. Case 9b (Windows-only) in tools/model-drift-test.cjs uses a stub run.

## Flow
- live run, engine timeout -> console.error -> NativeCommandError -> script ends
- fix: Continue around the native call; per-line UTF-8 log

## Expected impact
The scheduled run always ends with its own verdict and a readable log. Could break: nothing in CI (case skipped on Linux).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - the drift run survives a stderr line
Before: case 9b red: verdict never reached the log, script ended at stderr
After: green: both lines logged, exit 1 = run's, DRIFT printed; 11/11
Method: gate - red-then-green with a stub run
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence: probe: $ErrorActionPreference=Stop; & node -e "console.error(...)" 2>&1 | Tee-Object -> NativeCommandError, "reached the verdict" never printed

title: Decide the three owed desk layering breaks (meter/dataDir, twin store, docx zlib)
body:
## Summary
Three breaks of the desk layering are OWED in tools/desk-boundaries.cjs; each needs an owner ruling: fix, or allow with a reason.

## Description
engines/meter.ts loads lib/dataDir.ts (an engine reaching outside the seam for a leaf helper); twin/state.ts writes twin.json (a second store outside the session); rules/docx.ts imports node:zlib (a parser living in rules/). Allowing any is policy-loosen (widens what engines/rules/non-session code may do); fixing them edits the engines and essay-master contexts. Options: an ENGINE_DEPS allowance for leaf helpers, a WRITE_ALLOW entry or move behind session/, move docx.ts out of rules/.

## Flow
- owner rules on each -> the edit lands in its own context -> delete the OWED entry (the check fails until you do)

## Expected impact
Layering becomes fully green; the native rebuild (0003) inherits a clean seam.

## Evaluation
Claim: architecture - the stated layering holds with no exceptions
Before: 3 OWED breaks
After: 0 (per ruling)
Method: simulation - no instrument decides a policy
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: policy-loosen
evidence: tools/desk-boundaries.cjs OWED[0..2]; node tools/desk-boundaries.cjs -> 0 problems, 3 owed

title: .gitattributes checks deathride/gradlew.bat out with LF endings
instrument: a cmd probe: an LF-only copy of gradlew.bat with its goto labels shifted across a 512-byte boundary, run before/after `*.bat text eol=crlf`; plus git ls-files --eol on both wrappers
body:
## Summary
`* text=auto eol=lf` gives every .bat LF endings; deathride/gradlew.bat is LF in the working tree (root gradlew.bat is still CRLF only because its index copy was never normalized).

## Description
cmd.exe label search (goto/call) misreads LF-only batch files in edge cases, which is why Gradle's own .gitattributes sets `*.bat text eol=crlf`. Not reproduced here: the deathride wrapper runs today. Fix: `*.bat text eol=crlf` and renormalize the root wrapper.

## Flow
- a wrapper upgrade shifts a label across a 512-byte block -> goto fails on Windows

## Expected impact
Removes a latent Windows-only wrapper failure.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - batch files keep CRLF
Before: git ls-files --eol: deathride/gradlew.bat i/lf w/lf; gradlew.bat i/crlf w/crlf
After: both w/crlf
Method: simulation - the failure is not reproduced on today's files
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
.gitattributes:1 * text=auto eol=lf (no *.bat rule)
file deathride/gradlew.bat -> ASCII text (no CRLF)
